declarations.description:
A pivot table: it groups flat rows by the fields set on `rows` and `columns` and aggregates `values` in every cell,
with subtotals and totals, as a spreadsheet's pivot does.

Each `values` entry is `{ field, aggregate, label, format }`: the aggregate is `sum` (the default), `count`, `avg`,
`min`, `max` or `distinct`, and `format` takes `Intl.NumberFormat` options. Several values split each column. Row
groups expand and collapse (`expand-depth` sets how deep they start open), with a subtotal under each open group
(`subtotals`) and a grand total row and column (`totals`). Clicking a column header sorts the rows by it. `heatmap`
tints each cell by its value.

With `configurable`, a field list beside the grid lets the reader drag fields between rows, columns and values (or
move them from each field's menu) and change a value's aggregate; `pivot-change` gives the new layout.
`cell-click` gives the records behind a cell, for drill-down, and `toCSV()` exports what is shown. `pivot()` is the
same computation as a plain function.

For a financial statement, a `values` entry with `compute` and `of` is worked out from two other values of the same
cell (`{ "field": "variance", "compute": "difference", "of": ["actual", "budget"] }`; `percent-difference` and
`ratio` too), so subtotals and totals get the variance of their own sums. `invert-signs` flips the sign of the rows
in the named groups before aggregation (`{ "section": ["Expenses"] }`), so they subtract in the totals above them.
A computed cell carries the `negative` or `positive` class, coloured by the `__computed` variables.

The grid is a `treegrid`: the arrow keys move between cells, Left and Right close and open a group, and Enter on a
value cell fires `cell-click`.

declarations.name: AGING_BUCKET_FIELD
declarations.description: The field each record's bucket goes under: the one column field of an aging table, as `cell-click` names it.

declarations.name: agingDay
declarations.description: A date as a whole number of days since 1970-01-01: `YYYY-MM-DD` as written, any other date by its local calendar day.

declarations.name: agingBuckets
declarations.description:
The bucket keys for the given upper bounds, in order: `0` (not yet due), then `1-30`, `31-60`, … and `91+` for
`[30, 60, 90]`. Each key is what a cell's column path holds.

declarations.name: agingBucket
declarations.description: The bucket key of a number of days past due: `0` when not yet due.

An accounts receivable or payable aging table: one row per customer or vendor, a column per bucket of days past due
against an as-of date (Current, 1–30, 31–60, 61–90, Over 90), with row and column totals. It is
[`c2-pivot-table`](/web-components/components/pivot-table) with its columns fixed to those buckets: grouping,
subtotals, sorting, `heatmap`, `cell-click` for drill-down and `toCSV()` work as there.

Each record of `data` is an open item (an invoice or a bill) with a date to age from (`date-field`, `dueDate` by
default, a `YYYY-MM-DD` text, a timestamp or a `Date`) and an amount. The days past due are the whole days from that
date to `as-of` (today when empty); zero or fewer is Current. `buckets` sets the bounds (`30;60;90`); a record with
no date shows under "No date". Every bucket shows even when nothing falls in it.

`rows` groups the items (`customer` by default; `region;customer` nests them) and `values` sums their amount
(`[{ "field": "amount" }]` by default; give it a `format` for a currency). The columns are always the buckets:
`columns` is ignored, and `configurable` changes the rows and values only. `cell-click` names the bucket in
`columnPath` by its key (`0`, `1-30`, …, `91+`).

Amounts past due carry the `overdue` class and the last bucket `oldest`, coloured by the `__overdue` and `__oldest`
variables. The `as-of` line above the grid can be replaced through its slot, for example by a date field that sets
`as-of`.
